newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Nov 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Nov 20.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO -- Chief Executive candidate Tung Chee-hwa said that if he won the selection, he would legalise the Chinese Communist Party in Hong Kong if it asked.

-- Taiwanese President Li Teng-hui said he would like to meet Chinese President Jiang Zemin and hoped that Jiang would study more about the history of Taiwan and the pursuit of democracy by the Taiwanese people.

-- EXPRESS NEWS -- Director of Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office Lu Ping showed up at the World Economic Forum on Tuesday unexpectedly and briefly. The timing was scheduled carefully to avoid meeting Governor Chris Patten who arrived after Lu left.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- Chinese President Jiang said China and Russia should co-operate to build a new international political and economic order.
-- Jiang met German President Herman Herzog, saying Sino-Germnn relations had survived previous problems.

-- WEN WEI PO -- U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher arrived at Beijing, stressing the importance of Sino-U.S. relations. Beijing expressed its hope that relations would develop steadily and healthily.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES -- New World Infrastructure signed several construction project agreements with China's Tianjing municipal government, involving total investment of more than 20 billion yuan.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Swisshotel, the hotel division of Swissair, set up a headquarters in Hong Kong to oversee regional expansion.
-- Treasury bond prices plummeted as mainland banks and investors cashed in on the debt paper to take advantage of the stock market rally and to cover year-end financial positions.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Hong Kong's hnndover might further delay approval of China's permanent Most Favoured Nation trading status by the U.S. Congress, despite improving relations between Beijing and Washington.
